app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

final_report.root_cause: Client requests to the shipping Service (ClusterIP 10.96.175.51:8080) were receiving TCP connection refusals (ECONNREFUSED) even though at least one shipping pod and Service Endpoint were healthy and listening on :8080. The most likely root cause is a node-level service-proxying failure (kube-proxy / iptables or equivalent service NAT not translating the ClusterIP to the pod IP) on the node hosting the frontend-proxy and shipping pods. This caused connections made to the ClusterIP to hit no local listener and be refused. Direct proof (kube-proxy process logs or iptables/nft rules) was not collected during the investigation, so the exact process (kube-proxy crash, iptables/nft rules corruption, or CNI/node-networking regression) cannot be pinned with absolute certainty from the available evidence.
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Multiple traces from the frontend-proxy show outbound calls failing with 'connect: connection refused' / 'ECONNREFUSED 10.96.175.51:8080' when calling http://shipping:8080/get-quote. 2) Service/Endpoint inspection shows shipping Service has ClusterIP 10.96.175.51:8080 and Endpoints populated with pod IP 10.244.1.28:8080. 3) The shipping pod (shipping-fb896db58-24l6l) is Running, Ready, and its logs show it successfully bound to 0.0.0.0:8080 and served requests — no crashes, bind failures, or probe failures. 4) frontend-proxy and shipping pods are scheduled onto the same node (kind-worker) and there are no NetworkPolicy objects in the namespace that would block traffic. 5) frontend-proxy logs (collected at the available level) do not include explicit upstream-resolution/TCP error lines, but the traces clearly record connection refused to the Service ClusterIP. Together these facts indicate the application and Service endpoints were healthy while ClusterIP-based connections from the frontend-proxy were being refused, consistent with a node-level service proxy / iptables NAT failure.
final_report.investigation_summary: All planned RCA tasks were executed (priorities 1..7). Priority-1 checks verified Endpoints exist and at least one Ready pod backs the shipping Service. Priority-2 and -3 checks confirmed ports, service selectors, and DNS/service naming align between frontend-proxy and shipping. Priority-6 reviewed frontend-proxy logs (up to large tails) and found only Envoy startup messages and no explicit DNS or TCP error lines; however traces still show ECONNREFUSED to the ClusterIP. Priority-7 ruled out NetworkPolicy or missing sidecar as causes. With application, Service, and pod-level causes disproven, the remaining plausible failure domain is node-level service proxying (kube-proxy / iptables/nft / CNI host networking).
